competitive_landscape: The market today is private tenders, RIBs and charter yachts plus the Palau–Maddalena car ferry — premium but diesel and wake-heavy. There is no scheduled premium fast link and no zero-emission foiling option; the marine-park setting actively favours quiet, low-wake, emission-free craft, giving Navier a regulatory + experiential edge over conventional tenders.

All inside the 70 nm all-electric envelope; wake-light foiling is ideal for the national-park waters.

Same setting — a protected marine environment that mandates low-impact, zero-emission craft.

regulatory_note: Italian flag / EU regime; Capitaneria di Porto oversight; the La Maddalena Archipelago National Park imposes navigation and anchoring restrictions that favour low-impact, zero-emission, wake-light vessels — a direct advantage for a foiling craft. EU FuelEU Maritime adds emissions pressure.
seasonality: Intensely seasonal — Jun–Sep peak around the regatta and resort calendar, strong May/Oct shoulders; near-dormant winter. Peak-season charter day-rates are among the highest in the Med, supporting premium pricing.

summary: The Costa Smeralda in northeast Sardinia is one of the Mediterranean's most concentrated luxury yachting markets: Porto Cervo's marina is a global superyacht hub, ringed by ultra-premium resorts and villas, and it sits directly beside the La Maddalena archipelago — a protected national park of clear, sheltered channels and short island hops to Caprera, Spargi, Budelli and across to Bonifacio in Corsica. The combination of extreme willingness-to-pay, dense short legs and a marine-protected setting that penalises noise, wake and emissions is an almost ideal Navier fit: a quiet, wake-light, zero-emission foiling tender and day-charter craft is exactly what the park and the clientele want. Pioneer II owns the entire archipelago; Quanta-LR opens the longer Sardinia–Corsica–mainland legs.
tagline: Italy's premier superyacht base and a protected island archipelago — ultra-high willingness-to-pay meets a marine park that rewards zero-emission craft.
